paras: The killing of Dan Washington was the shooting death of Washington, a Black man, by Constable DeBerry in the court house at Fairfield, Texas, on the morning of April 6, 1903. The constable fired five times, and the one detailed report said Washington had threatened him but did not fire himself. The killing ran as a brief item in several Texas papers and one Louisiana paper.

According to a special from Fairfield to the Times-Herald, relayed from Waco, Washington and the constable met in the court house that Monday morning and the constable "opened fire." He shot five times, and the dispatch stated that "The negro did not fire." A separate telephone message from Fairfield said Washington was "instantly killed." The only explanation offered was that "It is claimed the constable had been threatened by the negro"; the dispatch did not say who made the claim or what the threat was.
No report of an inquest, arrest, grand-jury action or trial appears in the coverage.

The San Antonio Daily Light carried the Waco special on the day of the killing under the headline "CONSTABLE KILLS NEGRO. The Latter Had Threatened the Officer and Five Shots Fired." The headline stated the threat as fact, although the body of the story presented it only as a claim and noted that Washington did not shoot. Other papers reduced the story to a single line naming neither the shooter nor a cause.

A syndicated "News in Brief" digest printed the item in the Bryan Morning Eagle on April 11 and in the Shreveport Caucasian on April 12. The Shiner Gazette's "All Over Texas" column ran the telephone report on April 22 and repeated it on April 29. Every report identified Washington only as "a negro," and no Black newspaper account of the killing was found.

reader.title: Killing of Dan Washington
bases: The only account naming a shooter says a constable shot Washington five times in the court house after a claimed threat, with no crowd or mob reported (A1).

A Waco special (A1), a news digest (A2) and a telephone message from Fairfield (A4) agree that Dan Washington, a Black man, was shot five times and killed at Fairfield, though only A1 names the constable as the shooter and all may derive from the same Fairfield report.
